title: Physiological Hue-Heat effect despite absent multi-site perceptual effect
question: Does reddish versus bluish white lighting produce a reproducible change in skin temperature across laboratories even though the published multi-site analysis found no corresponding thermal-sensation effect?

competing_explanations.A_no_cross_modal_effect: Typical 3000-6000 K white-light CCT does not materially alter thermoregulation or thermal sensation under controlled room temperatures.
competing_explanations.B_hidden_physiological_effect: Light hue alters peripheral/mean thermoregulation, but the physiological effect is too small, variable, or weakly coupled to conscious thermal judgment to yield a multi-site sensation effect.

prior_art_gate.multi_site_perception: Bavaresco et al. 2026, Building and Environment 292:114264 reports no CCT effect on thermal sensation/preference across 8 labs.
prior_art_gate.physiology_prior_art: Single-site studies report mixed physiological results; a 2026 VR study found a hue effect on thermal sensation but not skin temperature. No cross-lab analysis of the open Annex 79 physiological arm was found in the discriminator-specific search.

evidence_roles.assignment_rule: odd/even laboratory ID, frozen before reading any CSV values

frozen_estimands.primary_physiology: within experimental round, reddish minus bluish difference in mean of available skin-temperature sites during a fixed terminal window of each lighting period; estimate lab effect while adjusting for lighting order and thermal condition
secondary_physiology: distal skin temperature: mean of hand and foot when both are available
frozen_estimands.perceptual_endpoint: within-round reddish minus bluish overall thermal-sensation vote
frozen_estimands.direction: B predicts reddish > bluish skin temperature

frozen_decision_rule.discovery: primary mean-skin-temperature effect must be positive in >=3/4 discovery labs; equal-weight one-sample t test across the four lab effects one-sided p<=0.025; pooled sign must survive leave-one-lab-out; otherwise stop before confirmation
frozen_decision_rule.confirmation: apply the identical primary analysis unchanged; require positive effect in >=3/4 confirmation labs; equal-weight one-sample t test across the four lab effects one-sided p<=0.025; leave-one-lab-out pooled effects all positive. Secondary outcomes cannot rescue a failed primary.
frozen_decision_rule.interpretation: A replicated primary effect would support a physiological cross-modal effect, not prove that it mediates thermal sensation. A null primary would support no detectable physiological Hue-Heat effect at these CCTs under this protocol.

calibration.lesson: laboratory is the replication/inference unit; inverse-variance participant-dominated pooling was rejected by calibration

stop_reason: Discovery labs do not share an anatomically comparable skin-temperature measurement, and no common heart-rate variable has adequate coverage across all four discovery labs. A pooled physiological Hue-Heat effect would therefore compare different biological quantities across laboratories.
